title: Best Facebook Ad Spy Tools 2026: Free & Paid Compared
summary: We tested the top Facebook ad spy tools for 2026: free options like Sprites Ads Library and Meta’s own library vs. paid platforms like BigSpy and Minea.
body_markdown:
A **Facebook ad spy tool** lets you spy on competitors’ Facebook ads: search every advertiser at once, see ads that have already stopped, filter by run length and engagement, and save what you find. The Meta Ad Library alone is not enough. It shows one advertiser at a time, has no performance filters, no saving and no analysis. We tested the free and paid options below and ranked them by what a single seat actually gets.

## How we tested


Each tool was run against the same three advertisers (a DTC brand, a B2B SaaS company and a dropshipping store) with the same questions: what is live, what has run longest, what stopped. We weighted **Facebook and Instagram depth** first, **filters that surface winners** second, **price for one seat** third, and **what happens after the search** last. Prices are list prices re-checked against each vendor’s own pricing page on September 14, 2026; most tools discount annual billing by 10 to 30 percent. Nothing in the table had moved since the previous check, including the two that anchor the range — BigSpy at $9/$99/$249 and AdSpy at $149 flat with no annual discount.


## The best Facebook ad spy tools in 2026


### 1. Sprites Ads Library: best free Facebook ad spy tool


Cursor’s live Meta creatives on the Sprites Ads Library, free and without a login.


**Price:** free, no login. **Best for:** anyone who wants the analysis done rather than a bigger haystack. The[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) reads the public Meta, Google and LinkedIn libraries every week and publishes one analysed page per advertiser. As of September 14, 2026 it covers **86 advertisers and 68,706 recorded ads** — 20,596 on Meta, 29,217 on Google and 18,893 on LinkedIn — with 61 of those advertisers carrying live Meta creatives. Each page gives you: live ad count, format mix, hooks and CTAs, landing-page destinations, days live, ads launched per week and an estimated spend range calculated using Sprites’ proprietary AI model. Browsing needs no account; full advertiser pages open with an email. The same Sprites copilot that reads a competitor’s ads can draft and launch your response on[Meta](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-ads-ai) or[Google](https://www.sprites.ai/google-ads-ai) .


**Weakness:** the index is tech and SaaS heavy, and keyword search across every advertiser is a copilot job rather than a search box. Start with the[Facebook ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/facebook-ad-examples) gallery.


### 2. Meta Ad Library: the free baseline


The Meta Ad Library: every active ad from any Page, free, and the source every spy tool reads.


**Price:** free. **Best for:** checking any single advertiser right now. The official library at facebook.com/ads/library shows every active ad from any Page across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads and WhatsApp, with its start date, platforms and an impression range. Search by advertiser or keyword, filter by media type and platform, and switch the country to an EU state to read reach, age and gender breakdowns and the targeting the advertiser chose.


**Weakness:** one advertiser at a time, no history for ordinary commercial ads outside the EU, no export, no engagement data and no analysis. Our step-by-step guide:[how to see competitors’ Facebook ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/how-to-see-competitors-facebook-ads) .


### 3. BigSpy: best value paid spy tool


BigSpy: the largest database at the lowest entry price.


**Price:** free plan (five queries a day), Basic $9, Pro $99 (about $69 annual, $1 three-day trial), Group $249 a month. **Best for:** solo advertisers and small teams who want a searchable multi-platform archive without a $149 commitment. BigSpy covers Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest and more, with filters for country, format, CTA, engagement, run time and industry, plus tracked ads and daily downloads.


**Weakness:** a dated interface and occasional stale data on small pages; the free plan is a taster, not a research tool.


**Looking for a BigSpy alternative?** AdSpy for Meta depth and comment search, Minea for product research, TrendTrack for a cleaner interface at a similar price.


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a BigSpy subscription.


### 4. AdSpy: deepest Facebook and Instagram archive


AdSpy: one flat price for the deepest Meta archive and comment search.


**Price:** $149 a month, flat, with a card-required trial and no annual discount. **Best for:** agencies and affiliate media buyers who live in the Meta archive. AdSpy is Facebook and Instagram only, with the largest ad database in the category and the one feature nobody else matches: searching ad *comments* . Filters cover likes, shares, comments, run time, landing-page domain, CTA, gender, age and country.


**Weakness:** the price. A single brand with a handful of competitors gets the same answers from BigSpy or the free tools.


**Looking for an AdSpy alternative?** BigSpy Pro ($99) is the closest like-for-like at a lower price; Minea if the question is which products sell; the Sprites Ads Library if you want the analysis done for free.


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a AdSpy subscription.


### 5. Minea: best for ecommerce and dropshipping


Minea: ad search paired with product, shop and influencer analysis.


**Price:** free lite tier (200 credits), Starter $49, Premium $99, Business $399 a month, about 30 percent off annually. **Best for:** dropshippers and ecommerce teams whose real question is “what should I sell?” Minea starts from products rather than advertisers: ad search across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Pinterest sits next to shop analysis, influencer placement tracking and a daily winning-products feed.


**Weakness:** credit metering. Heavy users burn through a plan quickly, and brand-level research is faster elsewhere.


**Looking for a Minea alternative?** TrendTrack or WinningHunter for the same product-first workflow without credits; BigSpy for a cheaper Facebook-only archive; Pipiads if TikTok leads.


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a Minea subscription.


### 6. Foreplay: best for creative teams


Foreplay: the best swipe file in the category, with competitor tracking and briefs on higher tiers.


**Price:** Basic $59, Workflow $175, Agency $459 a month, with a free trial. **Best for:** creative teams that need to get from research to a brief. The Chrome extension saves any ad from the Meta Ad Library or TikTok into boards with tags, transcripts and AI descriptions; Discovery searches the community library; Spyder tracks named competitors and alerts you to launches; Briefs turns saved ads into production briefs.


**Weakness:** it saves and organises ads far better than it finds them, and $59 a month is a lot for a bookmarking tool.


**Looking for a Foreplay alternative?** For discovery, BigSpy or the Sprites Ads Library; for creative analytics on your own account, Atria (from $129 a month, annual).


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a Foreplay subscription.


### 7. PowerAdSpy: best multi-network search


PowerAdSpy: Facebook alongside YouTube, Google, native and Reddit in one search.


**Price:** bundled by platform, from about $69 a month. **Best for:** media buyers who run Facebook alongside YouTube, Google or native. PowerAdSpy searches all of them from one interface with landing-page, CTA, engagement and demographic filters.


**Weakness:** Meta depth is below AdSpy’s, and the price climbs fast once you want every network.


**Looking for a PowerAdSpy alternative?** Anstrex for native and push, AdSpy for Meta depth, BigSpy for a cheaper multi-platform archive.


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a PowerAdSpy subscription.


### 8. Adbeat: best for display and programmatic


Adbeat: publisher placements and spend estimates for display, native and programmatic.


**Price:** Standard $249, Advanced $399 a month, Enterprise by quote. **Best for:** agencies and larger advertisers whose competitors spend on display, native and programmatic as well as Facebook. Adbeat shows where competitors’ ads run (publisher placements and networks), how long they have run, and estimated spend, with a year of history on Advanced and three on Enterprise.


**Weakness:** it is not a Facebook tool first, and the entry price is the highest on this list.


**Looking for an Adbeat alternative?** PowerAdSpy covers native and YouTube for a fraction of the price; Anstrex covers native and push for affiliates.


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a Adbeat subscription.


### 9. TrendTrack: the newest entrant worth testing


TrendTrack: ad spy and store tracking in one, the newest tool in this set.


**Price:** Starter $59, Pro $89, Business $149 a month (about 30 percent less annually), no free trial. **Best for:** ecommerce operators who want ad spy and store intelligence together. TrendTrack pairs a Facebook, Instagram and TikTok ad database with tracking of which Shopify stores are growing and what they are running, in a cleaner interface than the older tools.


**Weakness:** it is young. Independent reviews are thin outside Trustpilot, and the archive is smaller than BigSpy’s or AdSpy’s.


**Looking for a TrendTrack alternative?** Minea for the mature version of the same idea; WinningHunter ($49 to $249 a month, no credits) for the closest like-for-like.


**Free alternative:** the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives you analysed competitor ads without a TrendTrack subscription.


## Meta ad spy tools vs the Meta Ad Library


Every Meta ad spy tool here indexes the same Meta Ad Library, so the difference is not the ads but what you can do with them. The library answers “what is this Page running today?” A spy tool answers what needs history or scale: which ads a competitor ran last quarter, which advertisers use a given claim, which creatives have survived longest. To spy on Facebook ads campaigns at the campaign level, read the landing-page URLs: UTM and campaign parameters expose audience, funnel stage and market names that no library publishes.


## How to choose a Facebook ad spy tool


**Dropshipping and ecommerce.** Your question is “which product is selling?”, so pick a product-first tool: Minea, TrendTrack or WinningHunter, with BigSpy Basic ($9) as the budget archive. Pair it with the free Sprites Ads Library for brand-level reads of the stores you admire.


**SaaS and B2B.** Your competitors are named and few, and they advertise on LinkedIn and Google as much as on Meta. The Sprites Ads Library covers all three on one page per advertiser, with SaaS-heavy coverage, and a scheduled[competitor analysis](https://www.sprites.ai/competitor-analysis) in the copilot replaces the weekly manual check.


**Agencies.** Volume and seats matter: AdSpy for Meta depth, BigSpy Group for seats across platforms, Foreplay Agency for the brief workflow, Adbeat if clients spend on display.


## Beyond Facebook: TikTok ad spy and Google


For **TikTok ad spy** , the free TikTok Creative Center shows top ads by industry and region but cannot search a specific advertiser; Pipiads (from $49 a month) has the largest TikTok archive, and BigSpy, Minea and TrendTrack include TikTok. For Google, the free[Google Ads Transparency Center](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-ads-transparency-center) shows every verified advertiser’s Search, YouTube and Display ads for a year after they last ran. The Sprites Ads Library puts a competitor’s Google and LinkedIn ads on the same page as their Meta creatives. For swipe files and Chrome extensions, see our[ad library alternatives](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/the-best-facebook-ad-library-alternatives-in-2025) roundup.


Whichever tool you land on, the value is in what you do with the ads after you find them.[Analyze ad creative](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/analyze-competitor-ads-winning-hooks) element by element, sort the openings using the[ad hook styles](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/ad-hook-styles) taxonomy, and let[creative analytics](https://www.sprites.ai/creative-analytics) turn the pattern into the next batch of tests.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best free Facebook ad spy tool?


Sprites Ads Library and Meta’s own Ad Library are both free. Meta’s library shows every active ad but offers no performance filters, saving or analysis; Sprites Ads Library adds AI-powered analysis of competitor creatives, with hooks, CTAs, landing pages and run length per advertiser, and needs no login.


### Can you spy on competitors’ Facebook ad targeting?


No tool shows exact targeting settings. Ad libraries reveal creative, copy, formats and run dates, and the Meta Ad Library adds the selected location, age and gender only for ads delivered in the EU. Everywhere else you infer targeting from creative angles, languages, placements and the landing page; audience settings stay private to the advertiser.


### Is the Facebook Ad Library free?


Yes. The Meta Ad Library at facebook.com/ads/library is free and needs no account. It shows every active ad from any Page with its start date, platforms, an impression range and, for EU-delivered ads, reach and targeting.


### Is spying on competitor ads legal?


Yes. Ad libraries exist because of Meta’s transparency requirements, so everything they show is public by design, and spy tools index that public data. Looking, analysing and learning from competitor ads is ordinary market research. Copying creative, copy or trademarks is a different matter, so use what you find to build your own angles.


### What’s the best AdSpy alternative?


For a free AdSpy alternative, Sprites Ads Library covers Meta ad research with AI analysis and no login. Among paid tools, BigSpy ($9 to $99 a month) and Minea ($49 to $399) are the most common AdSpy replacements, depending on whether you need database volume or dropshipping-specific product data.
